scenes.text: Your feed was making fifty-one database queries just to show fifty posts. Claude got it down to two.
Here's what happened. One query fetched the posts. Then, for every single post, the code went back and asked: who wrote this? That's one, plus N.
Each of those is a round trip to the database. Eight milliseconds each, times fifty-one, is over four hundred milliseconds of pure waiting.
Claude's fix: collect all the author IDs first, then fetch every author in one single query. Two trips. Same data.
So whenever you spot a query inside a loop, that's your N plus one. Batch it.
